issues.location: naive equinumerosity-class argument before the Tarski--Scott definition
issues.finding: The text claims the class of all sets equinumerous with A never exists as a set, but for A empty it is the singleton containing the empty set. Its given unbounded-rank example addresses singleton A only.
issues.proposed_resolution: Qualify failure to nonempty A, use copies obtained by Cartesian product with arbitrarily high-rank singletons for general nonempty A, and state the empty exception.

translation_treatment: The target supplies the nonempty qualification, general unbounded-rank construction, and empty exception; it also localizes naif and Potter's chapter citation. The frozen source remains unchanged.
